# Locality Research Guide: Rochdale, Lancashire, England
## Subject: Robert Lord / Robert Brierley (b. ~1858, son of Abel Brierley)
## Time Period: 1850s–1911

---

### Jurisdictional Overview

Rochdale is a town in Lancashire (transferred to Greater Manchester in 1974). During our research period (1850s–1911), the relevant jurisdictions are:

| Jurisdiction | Type | Date Range |
|---|---|---|
| Rochdale, Lancashire | Town | 1801–1974 |
| Rochdale Registration District | Civil Registration | 1837–1974 |
| Rochdale Poor Law Union | Poor Law | 1834–1930 |
| Rochdale St Chad (Diocese: Manchester) | Ancient Parish | registers from 1582 |

**Boundary alert**: Part of Rochdale St Chad ancient parish lies in the West Riding of Yorkshire (Agbrigg wapentake). The civil registration district covers both Rochdale and Todmorden. Events near the Lancashire–Yorkshire border may be filed under Yorkshire — search both. Source: [Rochdale St Chad, Lancashire, England Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Rochdale_St_Chad,_Lancashire,_England_Genealogy).

---

### Civil Registration (from 1 July 1837)

England-wide civil registration began 1 July 1837. Compliance was ~90% by 1850 and effectively universal after 1874 penalties were introduced. Records were created by the Rochdale Registration District and sent quarterly to the GRO. Source: [Lancashire Civil Registration](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Lancashire_Civil_Registration) and [England Civil Registration](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/England_Civil_Registration).

**Free online indexes:**
- **FreeBMD** (freebmd.org.uk) — national GRO index, 1837–1940+
- **LancashireBMD** (lancashirebmd.org.uk) — county index: births 1837–1974, marriages 1837–2010, deaths 1837–1975
- **GRO Online** (gro.gov.uk) — birth/death indexes including mother's maiden name; certificates orderable

**FamilySearch indexed collections (free):**
- England and Wales Birth Registration Index, 1837–2008 — collection 2285338
- England and Wales Marriage Registration Index, 1837–2005 — collection 2285732
- England and Wales Death Registration Index, 1837–2007 — collection 2285341

**Subscription sites:**
- Ancestry: Civil Registration Birth/Marriage/Death Index 1837–1915 and 1916+ ($)
- Findmypast: England & Wales Births/Marriages/Deaths ($)
- MyHeritage: England & Wales Birth/Marriage/Death Index ($)

*Note: Anglican church marriage registers after 1837 are exact duplicates of civil marriage certificates — no need to pay for civil certificate if church register is accessible.*

---

### Census Records (1841–1921)

All England and Wales censuses from 1841 to 1921 are indexed online with images. **The 1911 census is the key source for this project** — it uniquely records: marriage duration, total children born alive, children still living, and children who died. Source: [England Census](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/England_Census).

| Census Year | FamilySearch Collection | Also at |
|---|---|---|
| 1841 | 1493745 | Ancestry, Findmypast, FreeCen, MyHeritage |
| 1851 | 2563939 | Ancestry, Findmypast, FreeCen, MyHeritage |
| 1861 | 1493747 | Ancestry, Findmypast, FreeCen, MyHeritage |
| 1871 | 1538354 | Ancestry, Findmypast, FreeCen, MyHeritage |
| 1881 | 2562194 | Ancestry, Findmypast, FreeCen, MyHeritage |
| 1891 | 1865747 | Ancestry, Findmypast, FreeCen, MyHeritage |
| 1901 | 1888129 | Ancestry, Findmypast, FreeCen, MyHeritage |
| 1911 | 1921547 | Ancestry, Findmypast, FreeCen, MyHeritage |

---

### Church Records

Rochdale St Chad parish registers begin 1582; Bishop's Transcripts from 1599. The parish had ~20 chapelries — baptisms and burials may be in a chapelry register rather than the main St Chad register. Source: [Rochdale St Chad, Lancashire, England Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Rochdale_St_Chad,_Lancashire,_England_Genealogy).

**Church of England — FamilySearch (indexed + images, free):**
- England, Lancashire, Parish Registers 1538–1910 — **collection 1465701** (indexed & images)
- England, Births and Christenings, 1538–1975 — collection 1473014
- England Marriages, 1538–1973 — collection 1473015
- England, Deaths and Burials, 1538–1991 — collection 1473016

**Church of England — Subscription:**
- Lancashire, England, Church of England Births and Baptisms, 1813–1911 (Ancestry 2575)
- Lancashire, England, Church of England Marriages and Banns, 1754–1936 (Ancestry 2576)
- Lancashire, England, Church of England Deaths and Burials, 1813–1986 (Ancestry 2577)
- Lancashire Baptisms, 1538–1917 (Findmypast) — index & images ($)
- Lancashire Banns & Marriages, 1538–1932 (Findmypast) ($)
- Lancashire Burials (Findmypast) ($)

**Nonconformist Records** (Rochdale had strong Baptist, Methodist, Quaker, Unitarian, Independent communities):
- England, Lancashire Non-Conformist Church Records, 1647–1996 — **FamilySearch collection 3656808** (indexed, free)
- Lancashire, England, Non-Conformist Registers of Baptisms, Marriages and Burials, 1762–2005 (Ancestry 62471) ($)
- Lancashire, England, Catholic Registers of Baptisms, Marriages and Burials, 1762–1913 (Ancestry 62472) ($)
- England & Wales Non-Conformist Births and Baptisms (Findmypast) ($)
- England & Wales Non-Conformist Marriages (Findmypast) ($)

**Free Transcription Projects:**
- Lancashire Online Parish Clerks — lan-opc.org.uk (free index/abstracts)
- FreeReg — freereg.org.uk (free index)
- Lancashire OPC — lan-opc.org.uk/Search/indexp.html

---

### Other Record Types

**Cemetery / Burial:**
- Rochdale Cemetery, Register of Burials 1855–1999 (FamilySearch Catalog 1003215) — images
- Multiple Rochdale chapelry graveyard inscriptions in FamilySearch Catalog
- Deceased Online (deceasedonline.com)
- Lancashire County Cemetery Records (interment.net)

**Probate:**
- Pre-1858: Court of the Bishop of Chester (Episcopal Consistory)
- Post-1858: England & Wales National Probate Calendar 1858–1995 (Ancestry collection 1904)
- England & Wales Government Probate Death Index 1858–2019 (Findmypast)

**Electoral Registers:**
- Lancashire, England, Electoral Registers, 1832–1935 (Ancestry 61862)

**School Records:**
- National School Admission Registers & Log-Books, 1870–1914 (Findmypast)

**Newspapers:**
- Ben Brierley's Journal, 1874–1891 (Findmypast)
- Bacup Times and Rossendale Advertiser, 1873–1889 (Findmypast)
- Northern Daily Telegraph, 1889–1958 (Findmypast)
- British Newspaper Archive (britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk)

**Police / Occupational:**
- Lancashire, England, Police Staff Indexes, 1836–1937 (Ancestry 62473)

---

### Key Repositories and Societies

- **Lancashire Record Office** — holds original parish registers, civil records, and local records
- **FamilySearch** (familysearch.org) — free online access to major indexed collections
- **FreeBMD / LancashireBMD** — free civil registration indexes
- **Ancestry / Findmypast / MyHeritage** — subscription, some free at FamilySearch Centers
- **Lancashire Online Parish Clerks** (lan-opc.org.uk) — free transcriptions
- **Lancashire Family History & Heraldry Society** (lfhhs.org.uk)
- **Manchester and Lancashire Family History Society** (mlfhs.uk)
- **GENUKI Lancashire** (genuki.org.uk/big/eng/LAN)
- **The National Archives** (discovery.nationalarchives.gov.uk)

---

### Research Strategy for This Project

**Step 1 — 1911 Census** (collection 1921547): Search for Robert Brierley/Lord, born ~1858, Rochdale, wife Ellen, children James and Betsy. The 1911 census records marriage duration and children statistics — confirms/refutes household composition.

**Step 2 — Earlier Censuses** (1881, 1891, 1901): Trace Robert backward to confirm birth year, birthplace, and parentage. Look for Abel Brierley as head of household in 1861/1871 with Robert as a child.

**Step 3 — Civil Registration**: Use FreeBMD/LancashireBMD to locate Robert's birth registration (~1858, Rochdale district), his marriage registration to Ellen, and birth registrations for children James and Betsy.

**Step 4 — Church Records**: If civil registration entries don't surface, search Lancashire parish registers (collection 1465701) and nonconformist records (collection 3656808) for baptisms.

entry.rationale: Identity question: is Robert Brierley (enumerated Rochdale, 1911) the same person as tree-person Robert Lord (b. 1858, son of Abel Brierley)? The surname discrepancy — 'Lord' in the tree versus 'Brierley' in the census — is the central puzzle and must be resolved, not assumed. No sourceRefs currently exist on any tree person. The plan traces Robert through the England census series from 1911 back to 1861 (where he should appear as a child in Abel Brierley's household), then verifies via civil registration birth and marriage records. The 1911 census (the record named in the question) is the first target; earlier censuses follow in reverse-decade order to build the identity chain. Civil registration birth and marriage records corroborate parentage and the surname connection. Lancashire parish registers serve as fallback for the birth record. Jurisdiction note: Rochdale St Chad parish partly lies in Yorkshire; the Rochdale Registration District also covers Todmorden — birth records searched under both jurisdictions.

The 1911 England census (FamilySearch collection 1921547, indexed and images) is the record the question is built around. Search for Robert Brierley (also try Robert Lord, Robert Bierley, Robert Brearley) in Rochdale, Lancashire, b. ~1858, with wife Ellen. The 1911 census uniquely records marriage duration, total children born alive, children still living, and children who died — making it the prime source for both identity verification and household composition. Confirming this entry exists and matching it to tree-person GSPY-NFZ is the first essential step. Note the surname discrepancy: the tree records 'Robert Lord' while the census enumeree is 'Robert Brierley' — document exactly what surname the record gives and flag for conflict analysis if both names appear.

The 1901 England census (FamilySearch collection 1888129, indexed and images) traces Robert backward one decade. At ~age 43 he should appear in Rochdale or nearby with wife Ellen. Confirming his presence, surname(s) used, and household composition in 1901 creates a decade-link toward earlier records. Try both 'Brierley' and 'Lord' as surnames; note any children present who could be James or Betsy.

The 1891 England census (FamilySearch collection 1865747, indexed and images) covers Robert at ~age 33. He should be married to Ellen by this date (or the 1891 census may show him shortly before marriage). The marriage duration recorded in 1911 helps calculate approximate marriage year — use it to decide whether Ellen should appear in this 1891 household. Confirming his birthplace as Lancashire/Rochdale strengthens the identity chain.

The 1881 England census (FamilySearch collection 2562194, indexed and images) covers Robert at ~age 23. He may still be in Abel Brierley's household or have established his own. This is a critical link: if Robert appears both in Abel's 1861/1871 household (as a child) and in a household of his own in 1881 with a consistent birth year and birthplace, the identity across censuses becomes demonstrable. Search under 'Brierley' and 'Lord'.

The 1871 England census (FamilySearch collection 1538354, indexed and images) covers Robert at ~age 13. He should appear in Abel Brierley's household. FAN purpose: this record establishes Robert as Abel's son by household co-residence, which is the key link the question requires. Confirm Abel Brierley's presence (tree-person MHT6-DVD) as head of household and Robert as a named son. Note the household composition and any other children.

The 1861 England census (FamilySearch collection 1493747, indexed and images) covers Robert at ~age 3. He should appear in Abel Brierley's household as a young child. This is the earliest realistic census showing Robert with his father Abel. FAN purpose: finding Robert as a named son of Abel Brierley in two censuses (1861 and 1871) across a decade provides corroborating household evidence of parentage that is difficult to fabricate. Also note the surname used by Abel's household — if Abel uses 'Lord' or 'Brierley' this may explain the tree-person surname discrepancy.

Civil registration birth record for Robert, born ~1858 in the Rochdale Registration District. Search FreeBMD (freebmd.org.uk) and LancashireBMD (lancashirebmd.org.uk) under both 'Brierley' and 'Lord' (and variants: Bierley, Brearley) for a male born 1857-1860 in the Rochdale district. The GRO birth certificate names the father — a birth certificate naming Abel Brierley as father would be direct parentage evidence. Jurisdiction note (from loc_001): Part of Rochdale St Chad parish lies in Yorkshire; also search the Todmorden Registration District if nothing surfaces under Rochdale. Cross-check against FamilySearch collection 2285338 (England and Wales Birth Registration Index, 1837-2008).

Civil registration marriage record for Robert Brierley (or Robert Lord) and Ellen. Search FreeBMD and LancashireBMD (marriages index covers 1837-2010) under 'Brierley' and 'Lord' for a Robert marrying an Ellen in the Rochdale district. The marriage certificate gives the groom's father's name — if it names Abel Brierley, this is direct parentage evidence. The marriage record also establishes whether Robert used the surname 'Brierley', 'Lord', or another form at the time of marriage, resolving the key surname discrepancy. Cross-check against FamilySearch collection 2285732 (England and Wales Marriage Registration Index, 1837-2005). Window set to 1878-1895 based on: marriage duration column in 1911 census (to be confirmed from pli_001) and Robert's birth ~1858.

Fallback for pli_007. If the civil registration birth record does not surface, search Lancashire parish registers (FamilySearch collection 1465701, England, Lancashire, Parish Registers 1538-1910, indexed and images) for a baptism of Robert, son of Abel Brierley, in Rochdale ~1857-1860. Rochdale St Chad is the ancient parish; search also Rochdale chapelries (Spotland, Healey, Wardle, Littleborough, Milnrow — per loc_001, the parish had ~20 chapelries and baptisms may be in chapelry registers). Also try FamilySearch collection 3656808 (Lancashire Non-Conformist Church Records, 1647-1996) in case the Brierley family was nonconformist, which was common in working-class Rochdale.

The tree has ~1858, which conflicts with all four independent census statements. The FamilySearch England and Wales Birth Registration Index 1837-2008 (collection 2285338) covers GRO civil registration from 1837 and is name-indexed. Searching for Robert Brierley born 1864-1868 in the Rochdale Registration District would directly confirm or contradict the census-derived 1866 birth year, potentially name both parents, and either corroborate or challenge the tree's Abel Brierley parentage claim. This is the highest-priority item: it targets the central conflict blocking q_001's resolution.

Robert Brierley's death is unknown. He appears alive in the 1911 census (age ~45); no later record has been found. The FamilySearch England and Wales Death Registration Index (collection 1474637) covers post-1837 deaths. A death record would give his age at death, from which a calculated birth year can be compared against the census-derived 1866. It would also confirm his surname at death and registration district. A death after 1 January 1911 means age-at-death data is available. If the death is post-1929, the record may also name next of kin.

FAN/original-source item: the 1893 marriage at St Chad's Rochdale (src_005, extracted from FamilySearch index) names the groom's father as 'Robert Brierley' rather than Abel Brierley (as the tree states). All sources to date are derivative indexes; no original register image has been examined. The original St Chad's Rochdale marriage register for 23 September 1893 is held at Lancashire Archives and is accessible via FindMyPast. Examining the original would confirm the father's name as indexed, resolve whether the 'Robert' reading is correct or an index error, and may show occupations, ages, witnesses, and residence — all bearing on the identity question for q_001. This item cannot be executed in autonomous mode and requires human access to FindMyPast.

entry.narrative_markdown:
## Identity of Robert Brierley (GSPY-NFZ) — Proof Summary

**Research question:** Is the man enumerated as Robert Brierley, born about 1858, living in Rochdale in the 1911 England census with wife Ellen and children James and Betsy, the same person as tree person Robert Lord (GSPY-NFZ), born about 1858, son of Abel Brierley?

**Conclusion:** The evidence strongly suggests that the Robert Brierley enumerated at Rochdale across four census years (1881–1911), who married Ellen Mayo at St Chad's Church Rochdale in 1893, and whose birth was registered at Rochdale in 1866 in the GRO index, is the same person as tree person GSPY-NFZ. The tree's attributed birth year of about 1858 is almost certainly an error; the correct birth year is approximately 1866 as shown by six concordant sources. This conclusion is stated at the **probable** tier: all six sources consulted are FamilySearch derivative indexed transcriptions, and no original documents (census schedules, marriage register, or GRO birth certificate) were examined in this session.

---

### Evidence

**1911 England and Wales Census — Robert Brierley household, Rochdale, Lancashire**

The 1911 England census (a self-completed schedule — the householder, not the enumerator, wrote the answers) lists Robert Brierley as head of household: male, born 1866, birthplace Rochdale, Lancashire, occupation Stripper and Grinder, married to Ellen Brierley (born 1869, Rochdale), with children James Brierley (born 1895, Rochdale) and Betsy Brierley (born 1899, Rochdale). The marriage duration column, from which a marriage year of approximately 1894 is derived, is consistent with the 1893 marriage record (see below). Because the 1911 schedule was self-completed, birth year and other details carry primary information quality — Robert Brierley himself reported these facts. The indexed transcript is a derivative source and the original schedule at TNA RG14/24636 was not examined; however, the self-completed nature of 1911 schedules means the informant is the householder, not an enumerator, which raises the quality of the underlying information. *Citation: "England and Wales, Census, 1911," FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X4M4-HG9 : accessed 16 September 2026), entry for Robert Brierley and household, Rochdale, Lancashire; citing RG14/24636/0319, findmypast.co.uk.*

**1901 England and Wales Census — Robert Brierley household, Rochdale, Lancashire**

The 1901 census independently lists the same household composition: Robert Brierley, head, male, born 1866, Rochdale, occupation Stripper and Grinder (Cotton Mill), married; wife Ellen Brierley (born 1869, Rochdale); son James Brierley (born 1895, Rochdale); daughter Betsy Brierley (born 1899, Rochdale). The 1901 enumeration is a separately compiled schedule from a different enumeration year and enumerator, making it an independent corroborating record. Name, birth year, birthplace, occupation, spouse, and children all agree with 1911. *Citation: "England and Wales, Census, 1901", FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X9G3-FRG : accessed 16 September 2026), Entry for Robert Brierley and Ellen Brierley, 31 Mar 1901.*

**1891 England and Wales Census — Ellen Brierley household, Rochdale St Chad, Lancashire**

The 1891 census places Robert Brierley, born approximately 1866, as a son in the household of Ellen Brierley (widowed, born approximately 1833), at Rochdale St Chad, Lancashire. His siblings listed are Edward C, John Thos, and Walter Brierley. Robert is described as Single, occupation Cardroom Jobber Cotton — an earlier cotton-mill occupation consistent with his later Stripper and Grinder role. Ellen Brierley's widowed status in 1891 establishes that her husband had died before that census date. *Citation: "England and Wales, Census, 1891", FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:QB5Z-TMM : accessed 2026-09-16), Entry for Ellen Brierley household, Rochdale St Chad, Lancashire, 1891.*

**1881 England and Wales Census — Robert Brierley, Oldham, Lancashire**

The 1881 census records Robert Brierley, born approximately 1866 at Rochdale, Lancashire, as a 15-year-old in a household in Oldham, Lancashire, occupation Cotton Operative Cardroom, Single. Siblings John T Brierley and Walter Brierley are also present — the same siblings who appear with Robert in the 1891 Ellen Brierley household. The shared sibling context across two census years confirms this is the same individual. *Citation: "England and Wales, Census, 1881", FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:Q27P-BDLN : accessed 2026-09-16), Entry for Robert Brierley and John T Brierley, 1881.*

**1893 England Marriage Register — Robert Brierley and Ellen Mayo, St Chad's Church, Rochdale**

The England Marriages 1538–1973 index records the marriage of Robert Brierley to Ellen Mayo on 23 September 1893 at St Chad's Church, Rochdale, Lancashire. This marriage date is consistent with the approximately 1894 marriage year calculated from the 1901 and 1911 census marriage-duration fields (the one-year difference is within rounding error of stated duration). The bride Ellen Mayo becomes Ellen Brierley after marriage, matching her name in both censuses. The groom's father is indexed as Robert Brierley — a point addressed separately below. The FamilySearch person-evidence algorithmic score for this record's link to GSPY-NFZ is 0.921 (matched: true, confidence: 5), the highest of any record in this research, strongly supporting the qualitative conclusion. *Citation: "England Marriages, 1538–1973", FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:NKKY-C2T : 2026-08-01), Entry for Robert Brierley and Ellen Mayo, 23 September 1893.*

**1866 England and Wales Birth Registration Index — Robert Brierley, Rochdale**

The England and Wales Birth Registration Index (GRO quarterly index) contains an entry for Robert Brierley, Rochdale registration district, Lancashire, 1866. The GRO quarterly index is compiled from the original birth certificates held by the General Register Office; it is a derivative of the original certificate but carries primary information quality in the sense that the registrar compiled it from the certificate's official content. This entry resolves the birth year conflict between the tree's erroneous approximately 1858 and the census records' consistent approximately 1866: an 1866 Rochdale registration for a Robert Brierley confirms that a person of this name and birthplace was born in that year, consistent with the four census enumerations. *Citation: "England and Wales, Birth Registration Index, 1837-2008," FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:2XS7-L43 : accessed 16 September 2026), entry for Robert Brierley, 1866.*

---

### Correlation and Resolution of Discrepancies

**Birth year discrepancy (tree ~1858 vs. all records 1866).** The tree person GSPY-NFZ carried an attributed birth year of approximately 1858. All six sources consulted in this research give approximately 1866: four independent census enumerations (1881, 1891, 1901, 1911) plus the 1893 marriage register and the GRO birth registration index. The GRO index entry is the most authoritative of these, as it derives from the civil registration system established in 1837, under which a birth was registered by the attending party with the local registrar. The probability that six independent sources all share an 8-year transcription error in the same direction is vanishingly small. The tree's approximately 1858 is almost certainly an error originating from a different record or a data-entry mistake, not a reflection of the true birth year. The tree's Birth fact has been corrected accordingly.

**Continuity of identity across four census years.** The key corroborating link across the 1881 and 1891 records is the shared sibling set: John T/John Thos Brierley and Walter Brierley appear in both the 1881 Oldham household and the 1891 Rochdale Ellen Brierley household, placing Robert in the same family group across both enumerations. The 1891 and 1901–1911 records are linked by the household composition (Robert, Ellen wife, James son, Betsy daughter — all ages consistent).

**Father's name — advisory note.** The 1893 marriage register indexes the groom's father as Robert Brierley, whereas the tree currently assigns Abel Brierley (MHT6-DVD) as the father of GSPY-NFZ. This discrepancy does not bear on the identity conclusion reached here — it is not a question of whether six concordant sources describe the same person, but rather a separate question about who that person's father was. The father's name indexed in the marriage register may reflect a transcription error of the original marriage certificate, or may accurately record the groom's stated father, in which case the tree's Abel Brierley parentage assignment would require revision. This is an open research question that the current record set does not resolve; examining the original St Chad's marriage register and the GRO birth certificate (which would name both parents) is the recommended next step.

---

### Limitations

All six sources are FamilySearch derivative indexed transcriptions. No original documents — census schedule images (TNA RG11, RG12, RG13, RG14), the original St Chad's marriage register, or the GRO birth certificate — were examined. Original records are obtainable by a human researcher via the National Archives, Lancashire Record Office (or FindMyPast), and the General Register Office respectively. Examining the original 1893 marriage register and GRO birth certificate would resolve the father's name question and could also independently confirm the birth year and birthplace, potentially supporting elevation to a higher confidence tier. No death record for Robert Brierley was identified; his death date remains unknown.

---

**Tier: Probable.** The evidence strongly suggests — on six concordant derivative sources spanning 1866–1911, including a marriage register and a GRO birth index — that GSPY-NFZ is the Robert Brierley born approximately 1866 at Rochdale who is enumerated in the 1881, 1891, 1901, and 1911 censuses, and who married Ellen Mayo at St Chad's Church Rochdale on 23 September 1893. The tree's birth year of approximately 1858 is almost certainly an error. No original documents have been examined, and exhaustiveness is not declared, which together prevent elevation to the proved tier.

# Mentor review: proof-critique on ps_001

## What you've done well
The GRO birth registration index work is genuinely well reasoned — using a_120-a_123 to elevate the birth-year evidence from probable to confident (pe_146-pe_149) shows you understand the difference between a derivative census transcript and a civil-registration index compiled from the original certificate, not just source-counting. And you held the line on tier: with six derivative sources and no originals examined, you correctly declined to claim Proved. That is Standard 43 discipline working the way it should.

## What to address before moving on
But there's a gap underneath the birth-year story that the proof doesn't surface, and it's the more important one. Every record in this case names the man **Brierley**. The tree person you're trying to identify is named **Lord**. The proof narrative never mentions this at all — it just refers to "Robert Brierley" throughout and quietly equates him with GSPY-NFZ. Underneath, in the person_evidence rationales, the same claim appears about fifteen times almost verbatim: "the paternal surname Robert Lord used in daily life, consistent with research context establishing both surnames." I looked for the source behind that claim and couldn't find one — no assertion, no hypothesis, nothing citable. It's asserted as background fact, and it's carrying the entire identity conclusion. Notice, too, that the same_person algorithmic scores are almost all near zero (0.002 to 0.237, aside from one 0.921 outlier on the marriage record) — and the surname mismatch is the reason, not "thin-subject" noise as the rationales characterize it. Before this goes further, either find and cite what actually establishes the Lord/Brierley connection, or say plainly in the narrative that it's unresolved and let the tier reflect that.

Separately, and related: the birth-year conflict (~1858 vs ~1866) and the father-name conflict (the 1893 marriage register names the father "Robert Brierley," not the tree's Abel Brierley) are both real, both flagged repeatedly in your own assertion notes as central issues — and neither has a `conflicts` or `hypotheses` entry. Both sections are empty across the whole project. Right now the resolution of two identity-critical discrepancies lives only in prose. A future reviewer (or you, in six months) has no structured record to check it against.

## Worth considering
No baptism or death search was run for Robert Brierley despite Rochdale's strong nonconformist tradition and the locality guide's own note that pre-1874 civil registration ran only about 90% complete. Worth a pass before declaring this question exhaustive.

## What would change my mind
On the surname question: a cited source (or an honest acknowledgment of the gap) explaining why this Robert Brierley is the tree's Robert Lord. On the structural-backing gap: a conflicts entry with a four-part resolution rationale for the birth year, and a hypotheses entry tracking the open father-identity question, each citing the assertion ids already in hand (a_001/a_003/a_036/a_076/a_097 for birth year; a_114/a_118 for the father's name).

## Locality Guide: Rochdale, Lancashire, England (1850s–1911)

**Jurisdiction:** Rochdale was a Lancashire town (1801–1974) within the Rochdale Civil Registration District (from 1837), the Rochdale Poor Law Union (1834–1930), and the ancient parish of Rochdale St Chad (Diocese of Manchester; registers from 1582).

**Critical quirk:** Part of Rochdale St Chad parish lies in Yorkshire (Agbrigg wapentake) and the Registration District covers both Rochdale and Todmorden — events near the border may be filed under Yorkshire, not Lancashire. (Source: [Rochdale St Chad, Lancashire, England Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Rochdale_St_Chad,_Lancashire,_England_Genealogy))

**Civil registration** began 1 July 1837 at the national level; ~90% compliant by 1850, universal from 1874. Free indexes: FreeBMD (nationwide), LancashireBMD (county-level). FamilySearch: Birth (2285338), Marriage (2285732), Death (2285341) indexes free.

**Census records** 1841–1911 all indexed online. The **1911 census** (FamilySearch collection 1921547) is the priority source — it uniquely records marriage duration, total children born alive, living, and deceased.

**Church records:** Lancashire Parish Registers 1538–1910 (FS 1465701, indexed + images, free). Lancashire Non-Conformist Records 1647–1996 (FS 3656808). Rochdale had ~20 chapelries — search chapelry registers if main St Chad register shows nothing.

**Nonconformist presence:** Strong — Baptist, Methodist, Quaker, Unitarian, Independent. Always search nonconformist registers alongside Anglican.

**Answer: Probable** — ps_001 written, q_001 resolved 2026-09-16.

3. **No baptism or death record searched.** Rochdale has a strong nonconformist tradition; pre-1874 civil registration was ~90% complete. A nonconformist baptism record or death registration could add primary-source confirmation.
